body.statement:
For an admissible fixed choice of class constants with \(H=0\), \(p=S=d=1\), \(\lambda=\kappa=1\), and the uniform order-zero kernel \(K\), there is a triangular array of laws in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\), with \(n_1=N=T^2\), for which
\[
R_\star=T^{-2},
\qquad
\lim_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0\right]=\frac{3}{16}.
\]
Moreover, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
body.proof_tex:
It suffices to exhibit one admissible triangular array.  Fix
\[
H=0,\qquad p=S=d=1,\qquad \lambda=\kappa=1,
\qquad \pi_1=1,
\]
and choose
\[
B=16,\qquad c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1,
\qquad \delta_0=\frac14,
\qquad c_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}=1.
\]
Take the H\"older radius \(L\) large enough to contain the affine regression below, let
\(K(u)=\mathbf 1\{|u|\leq1\}\), and use an admissible normalized-shape threshold
\(0<c_G\leq1\).  Because \(\lambda=1\), the prescribed local-polynomial degree is
\(r=0\) and \(b_0(u)=e_0=1\).  Let \(E_0\) be constant, set
\(z_0=1/2\), and put \(\mathcal Z_+=\{1/2\}\).  For every integer \(T\geq1\), set
\[
n_1=N=T^2.
\]

Write \(X_t=X_{1t}\).  Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_T\) be independent uniform random variables on
\([0,1]\), and define
\[
m(x)=8+x-\frac12,
\qquad
Q_{1ti}=m(X_t)+\frac12U_{ti},
\]
where the variables \((U_{ti})_{t,i}\) are independent Rademacher variables and are independent of the complete design.  Since \(m([0,1])=[15/2,17/2]\),
\[
7\leq Q_{1ti}\leq9\leq B,
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[Q_{1ti}\mid X_t,E_0]=m(X_t)
\]
for every \(i\).  Thus the bounded-response and common conditional-mean requirements hold.  The design density equals one.  Moreover, the design process is independent over calendar time, so its conditional absolute-regularity coefficient is
\[
\beta_P(\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\mid E_0)=0
\qquad(\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\geq1),
\]
which satisfies the geometric design-only mixing restriction for any admissible positive envelope and decay constants.

Independently of the historical sample, let
\[
Z_j=\frac12+V_j,
\]
where \(V_1,\ldots,V_N\) are independent Rademacher variables.  Then
\[
\mathbb E_P[Z_j\mid E_0]=z_0,
\qquad
\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_j\mid E_0)=1,
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid E_0]=1\leq B.
\]
Hence donor replication, donor independence, ellipticity, and the fourth-moment envelope all hold.  Set \(X_{1t}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_t\), verifying exact observation of every training coordinate.

For \(0<\delta\leq\delta_0\), the points \(z_0+u\) with \(|u|\leq\delta\) remain in \([0,1]\), and \(\Sigma=1\).  Consequently the local modulus in \texttt{def:local-modulus} is
\[
\omega_P(\delta;z_0)
=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|m(z_0+u)-m(z_0)|
=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|u|
=\delta.
\]
Thus the two-sided modulus holds with the displayed constants.  The affine function \(m\) belongs to
\(\mathcal H_1(1,L)\),
\(\operatorname{dist}(z_0,\partial[0,1])=1/2\geq\delta_0\), and
\(P\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\geq c_X\).

Define the design-measurable event shock and the potential event outcomes by
\[
G=\mathbf 1\{X_1\leq1/4\},
\qquad
B_{1i}(0)=8,
\qquad
B_{1i}(1)=8+G,
\qquad
B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1).
\]
Set \(B_{1i}(a,\mathbf a_{-1i})=B_{1i}(a)\), and define
\(Q_{1ti}(a)=Q_{1ti}\) for both values of \(a\).  These equations establish event consistency, historical consistency, no spillovers, limited anticipation, and both wealth support conditions.  The buy-and-hold definition is realized by taking
\[
W_{1i,-1}=1,
\qquad
R_{1i0}(a)=B_{1i}(a)-1>-1,
\]
because then \(W_{1i,-1}\{1+R_{1i0}(a)\}=B_{1i}(a)\).  Since \(m(z_0)=8\), event transport follows from
\[
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E_P[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]=8=m(z_0).
\]
Conditional on the complete design and \(E_0\), all event outcomes are constants, while the historical path of unit \(i\) is a measurable function of the independent vector
\((U_{ti})_{t=1}^T\).  Therefore the unit paths are conditionally independent across \(i\), as required.  This verifies every maintained member property of
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(1)\); no within-site equality in distribution or conditional variance lower bound is used.

Because \(z_0\) and \(E_0\) are constant and \(P(G=1)=1/4\), the target definition gives
\[
\tau_n(z_0)
=\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E_P[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[G]
=\frac14,
\qquad
\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}=8+G.
\]

We next analyze the one-center estimator.  Put
\[
\bar Z=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^NZ_j,
\qquad
\widetilde z=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\bar Z).
\]
Projection onto the closed interval is nonexpansive and fixes \(z_0\), whence
\[
|\widetilde z-z_0|
\leq\left|\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^NV_j\right|,
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde z-z_0)^2\mid E_0]\leq\frac1N=T^{-2}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), the initial bandwidth in
\texttt{def:feasible-estimator} equals
\[
\underline h_T
=C_h\left[(Tn_1)^{-1/3}
\vee\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T
\vee N^{-1/2}\right]
=C_h\frac{\log T}{T}<1.
\]
Let
\[
I_T=\{t:|X_t-\widetilde z|\leq\underline h_T\},
\qquad
\mathcal A_T=\{|I_T|>0\}.
\]
For every fixed \(\widetilde z\in[0,1]\), the intersection of
\([\widetilde z-\underline h_T,\widetilde z+\underline h_T]\) with \([0,1]\) has Lebesgue measure at least \(\underline h_T\).  Donor independence and the uniform design imply
\[
P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0,\widetilde z)
\leq(1-\underline h_T)^T
\leq\exp(-T\underline h_T)
=T^{-C_h}.
\]
Thus \(P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\to0\).  On \(\mathcal A_T\), the order-zero local mass and Gram matrix at the initial bandwidth satisfy
\[
L_1=n_1|I_T|,
\qquad
G_1=n_1|I_T|,
\qquad
\lambda_{\min}(G_1/L_1)=1\geq c_G.
\]
Hence the normalized-shape rule selects \(h_1=\underline h_T\), and the fitted untreated value is
\[
\widehat m_1
=\frac1{n_1|I_T|}\sum_{t\in I_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Q_{1ti}.
\]
The conditional-mean part of this average differs from \(m(z_0)=8\) by at most
\(\underline h_T+|\widetilde z-z_0|\).  Conditional on the design and donors, its error part has mean zero and variance
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(
\frac1{2n_1|I_T|}\sum_{t\in I_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}U_{ti}
\,\middle|\,(X_t)_{t=1}^T,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N
\right)
=\frac1{4n_1|I_T|}
\leq\frac1{4n_1}.
\]
On a successful order-zero fit, \(\widehat m_1\in[0,B]\), and the definition sets the failed-fit contribution to zero.  The preceding bounds therefore yield, for a constant \(C\) independent of \(T\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_1-8)^2\mid E_0]
\leq C\left(\underline h_T^2+N^{-1}+n_1^{-1}
+P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\right)
\longrightarrow0.
\]

The raw estimator consequently satisfies
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=G-\frac14-\{\widehat m_1-m(z_0)\}.
\]
Writing \(D_T=\widehat m_1-m(z_0)\), expansion of the square gives
\[
\left|
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
-\mathbb E_P[(G-1/4)^2\mid E_0]
\right|
\leq
2\{\mathbb E_P[(G-1/4)^2]\}^{1/2}
\{\mathbb E_P[D_T^2\mid E_0]\}^{1/2}
+\mathbb E_P[D_T^2\mid E_0],
\]
where the inequality is Cauchy--Schwarz.  Its right-hand side tends to zero, while
\(G\) is Bernoulli with success probability \(1/4\).  Hence
\[
\lim_{T\to\infty}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
=\operatorname{Var}_P(G)
=\frac14\left(1-\frac14\right)
=\frac3{16}.
\]

The four iid-comparator terms in \texttt{def:rate-frontier} are, exactly,
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}=n_1^{-1}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sm}}=(Tn_1)^{-2/3}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}=T^{-2}.
\]
Therefore \(R_\star=T^{-2}\).

It remains to show the failure of the full-data interval.  On \(\mathcal A_T\), the successful local-constant weights are
\[
a_{1ti}=\frac{\mathbf 1\{t\in I_T\}}{n_1|I_T|},
\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^T|a_{1ti}|=\frac1{n_1},
\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}|a_{1ti}|=1.
\]
Thus, for fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), the two Hoeffding radii obey
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}}\right)
\frac1{n_1}\right\}^{1/2}
=O(T^{-1}),
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}}\right)
\frac1{n_1}\right\}^{1/2}
=O(T^{-1}).
\]
Nonnegativity, unit total weight, and kernel support give the exact Taylor allowance bound
\[
A_L
\leq C_{0,1}L\underline h_T
=O\!\left(\frac{\log T}{T}\right).
\]

For completeness, the full-sample donor calibration is valid directly in this array.  Here \(D=1\), \(Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)=V_j\), and independence with zero mean gives
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\left|N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^NY_j\right|^4
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]
=3-\frac2N
\leq \frac{16}{N}+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(1^2+2\cdot1)
=M_4(N).
\]
With \(q_N=\{M_4(N)/\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\}^{1/4}\), Markov's inequality therefore gives
\[
P\!\left\{
\left|N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^NY_j\right|>q_N
\,\middle|\,E_0\right\}
\leq\frac{M_4(N)}{q_N^4}
=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Projection contraction and \(c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\) imply on the complementary event that
\[
|\widetilde z-z_0|
\leq\frac{q_N}{\sqrt N}
=\delta_N.
\]
Moreover,
\[
M_4(N)=\frac{16}{N}+3\left(1-\frac1N\right)\leq16,
\qquad
q_N=O(1),
\qquad
\delta_N=O(T^{-1}),
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{don}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_N^\kappa=O(T^{-1}).
\]
In particular, \(\delta_N\leq\delta_0\) for all sufficiently large \(T\).

On \(\mathcal A_T\), the sole Gram matrix is positive, all weights and radii are finite, and the donor-radius condition holds for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Hence the bad-sample event in \texttt{def:honest-interval} is contained in \(\mathcal A_T^c\) eventually.  On \(\mathcal A_T\),
\[
H_\alpha
=R_{\mathrm{hist}}+R_{\mathrm{evt}}+A_L+A_{\mathrm{don}}
=O\!\left(\frac{\log T}{T}\right)
=o(1).
\]
If the nonfallback interval contains \(\tau_n(z_0)\), then
\(|\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)|\leq H_\alpha\).  But
\(|G-1/4|\geq1/4\) almost surely and
\(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)=G-1/4-D_T\).  Therefore, once the deterministic bound on \(H_\alpha\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A_T}\) is below \(1/8\),
\[
\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\}
\subseteq
\mathcal A_T^c\cup\{|D_T|\geq1/16\}.
\]
Indeed, outside the displayed union the reverse triangle inequality gives
\(|\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)|\geq1/4-1/16=3/16>1/8\).  Consequently
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
\leq P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)
+P(|D_T|\geq1/16\mid E_0)
\longrightarrow0,
\]
where the second term tends to zero because
\(\mathbb E_P[D_T^2\mid E_0]\to0\).  This proves the amended proposition.
